text: Why can a non-volatile phase-change-material (PCM) synapse be attractive for deployed fixed-weight inference despite its costly write?
choices: Because its write energy is sub-femtojoule, cheaper than any spike
Because a write costs about a nanojoule but the weight then holds at zero static power, so for fixed-weight inference the write energy amortizes to nearly nothing
Because PCM synapses must be rewritten before every spike
Because PCM continuously draws power to hold its state, guaranteeing stability
explanation: A PCM write is relatively expensive (about a nanojoule to crystallize or amorphize the film), but the state is non-volatile and holds at zero static power, so for deployed fixed-weight inference that one-time write amortizes away. The write is nanojoule-scale, not sub-fJ (option 0), the state persists without rewriting (option 2), and it holds at zero, not continuous, power (option 3).
